```plato
//==
// # Matrix operations
//
// The portable reference bodies for `Matrix3x2` (2D affine) and `Matrix4x4`
// (3D homogeneous), covering determinant, inversion, arithmetic, decomposition,
// and the whole `Create*` construction family. These used to be bodiless
// intrinsics; the semantics here match System.Numerics `Matrix3x2` / `Matrix4x4`
// element for element, so a backend may substitute the native call.
// Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Matrices (row-vector multiplication, v' = v M).
//
// Element naming follows the row-vector layout of `matrices.types.plato`: for
// Matrix3x2, M11 = Row1.X ... M32 = Row3.Y and Row3 is the translation; for
// Matrix4x4, M11 = Row1.X ... M44 = Row4.W and Row4 is the translation.
//
// Two deliberate deviations from the System.Numerics reference implementation:
//
//   * `Matrix3x2.CreateRotation` does NOT snap angles within a thousandth of a
//     degree of a multiple of a quarter turn to exact 0 / +-1 cosines. Plain
//     Cos / Sin are used instead: the snap is a C#-era numerical courtesy, not
//     part of the mathematical definition, and it costs a per-call
//     IEEERemainder plus four range tests on every backend.
//   * The projection and view constructors (`CreatePerspective*`,
//     `CreateOrthographic*`, `CreateLookAt`, `CreateWorld`) throw
//     ArgumentOutOfRangeException in C# for degenerate inputs. Plato has no
//     exceptions, so the preconditions stated in each doc comment are UNCHECKED:
//     violating one yields infinities or NaN rather than a diagnostic.

library MatricesOps
{
    //==
    // # Matrix3x2 — the 2D affine map
    //
    // Three Number2 rows: a 2x2 linear block (Row1, Row2) plus a translation row
    // (Row3). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_transformation

    // The determinant of the 2x2 linear block: M11 M22 - M21 M12. The
    // translation row does not affect it.
    Determinant(self: Matrix3x2): Number
        => self.Row1.X * self.Row2.Y - self.Row2.X * self.Row1.Y;

    // The 3x2 matrix with every element NaN: what a failed inversion returns,
    // matching System.Numerics.
    NotANumber(_: Matrix3x2): Matrix3x2 {
        var n = 0.0 / 0.0;
        return (Number2(n, n), Number2(n, n), Number2(n, n));
    }

    // The inverse affine map, paired with whether one exists. The linear block is
    // inverted by the 2x2 adjugate and the translation row carried back through
    // it. When the determinant is smaller than Number.Epsilon the matrix is
    // singular: the all-NaN matrix and `false` are returned.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertible_matrix
    Invert(self: Matrix3x2): Tuple2<Matrix3x2, Boolean> {
        var m11 = self.Row1.X;
        var m12 = self.Row1.Y;
        var m21 = self.Row2.X;
        var m22 = self.Row2.Y;
        var m31 = self.Row3.X;
        var m32 = self.Row3.Y;
        var det = m11 * m22 - m21 * m12;
        var invDet = 1.0 / det;
        var inverse = Matrix3x2(
            Number2(m22 * invDet, -m12 * invDet),
            Number2(-m21 * invDet, m11 * invDet),
            Number2((m21 * m32 - m31 * m22) * invDet, (m31 * m12 - m11 * m32) * invDet));
        var ok = det.Abs >= Number.Epsilon;
        return (ok ? inverse : Matrix3x2.NotANumber, ok);
    }

    // Element-wise sum.
    Add(value1: Matrix3x2, value2: Matrix3x2): Matrix3x2
        => (value1.Row1 + value2.Row1,
            value1.Row2 + value2.Row2,
            value1.Row3 + value2.Row3);

    // Element-wise difference.
    Subtract(value1: Matrix3x2, value2: Matrix3x2): Matrix3x2
        => (value1.Row1 - value2.Row1,
            value1.Row2 - value2.Row2,
            value1.Row3 - value2.Row3);

    // Composition of two affine maps: applying the result is applying value1
    // then value2. The translation row of value1 is carried through value2's
    // linear block and then offset by value2's own translation.
    Multiply(value1: Matrix3x2, value2: Matrix3x2): Matrix3x2
        => (Number2(value1.Row1.X * value2.Row1.X + value1.Row1.Y * value2.Row2.X,
                    value1.Row1.X * value2.Row1.Y + value1.Row1.Y * value2.Row2.Y),
            Number2(value1.Row2.X * value2.Row1.X + value1.Row2.Y * value2.Row2.X,
                    value1.Row2.X * value2.Row1.Y + value1.Row2.Y * value2.Row2.Y),
            Number2(value1.Row3.X * value2.Row1.X + value1.Row3.Y * value2.Row2.X + value2.Row3.X,
                    value1.Row3.X * value2.Row1.Y + value1.Row3.Y * value2.Row2.Y + value2.Row3.Y));

    // Every element scaled, translation row included.
    Multiply(value1: Matrix3x2, scalar: Number): Matrix3x2
        => (value1.Row1 * scalar, value1.Row2 * scalar, value1.Row3 * scalar);

    // Every element scaled, with the scalar on the left.
    Multiply(scalar: Number, value1: Matrix3x2): Matrix3x2
        => value1 * scalar;

    // Every element divided. Matches System.Numerics: the reciprocal is formed
    // once and multiplied through.
    Divide(value1: Matrix3x2, scalar: Number): Matrix3x2
        => value1 * (1.0 / scalar);

    // Exact element-wise equality. Two matrices differing only by floating-point
    // drift compare unequal.
    Equals(a: Matrix3x2, b: Matrix3x2): Boolean
        => a.Row1.X == b.Row1.X && a.Row1.Y == b.Row1.Y
        && a.Row2.X == b.Row2.X && a.Row2.Y == b.Row2.Y
        && a.Row3.X == b.Row3.X && a.Row3.Y == b.Row3.Y;

    // Element-wise linear interpolation; `amount` is unclamped. Interpolating
    // rotations this way shrinks them toward the chord — decompose first if the
    // intermediate matrices must stay rigid.
    Lerp(self: Matrix3x2, matrix2: Matrix3x2, amount: Number): Matrix3x2
        => (self.Row1 + (matrix2.Row1 - self.Row1) * amount,
            self.Row2 + (matrix2.Row2 - self.Row2) * amount,
            self.Row3 + (matrix2.Row3 - self.Row3) * amount);

    // The combined hash of the three rows.
    Hash(self: Matrix3x2): Integer
        => self.Row1.Hash.CombineHash(self.Row2.Hash).CombineHash(self.Row3.Hash);

    //==
    // # Matrix3x2 construction

    // The affine map that shifts by `position` and does nothing else.
    CreateTranslation(_: Matrix3x2, position: Vector2D): Matrix3x2
        => (Number2(1.0, 0.0), Number2(0.0, 1.0), Number2(position.X, position.Y));

    // The uniform scale about the origin.
    CreateScale(_: Matrix3x2, scale: Number): Matrix3x2
        => (Number2(scale, 0.0), Number2(0.0, scale), Number2(0.0, 0.0));

    // The per-axis scale about the origin.
    CreateScale(_: Matrix3x2, scales: Number2): Matrix3x2
        => (Number2(scales.X, 0.0), Number2(0.0, scales.Y), Number2(0.0, 0.0));

    // The per-axis scale about `centerPoint`, which stays fixed. The translation
    // row is the offset that returns the scaled center to where it started.
    CreateScale(_: Matrix3x2, scales: Number2, centerPoint: Point2D): Matrix3x2
        => (Number2(scales.X, 0.0),
            Number2(0.0, scales.Y),
            Number2(centerPoint.X * (1.0 - scales.X), centerPoint.Y * (1.0 - scales.Y)));

    // The counter-clockwise rotation about the origin.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotation_matrix
    // Deviation: no quarter-turn snapping (see the file header).
    CreateRotation(_: Matrix3x2, angle: Angle): Matrix3x2 {
        var c = angle.Cos;
        var s = angle.Sin;
        return (Number2(c, s), Number2(-s, c), Number2(0.0, 0.0));
    }
```
